name: RNA therapeutics and next-generation vaccines
summary: RNA-based medicines change protein production or teach the immune system to recognise a target without permanently rewriting DNA.
useCase: A patient receives an RNA-silencing medicine for a defined disease, or a vaccine designed around a pathogen or tumour target.
whyNow: Commercial RNA interference has expanded sharply while vaccines and RNA editing progress through distinct clinical paths. Pandemic vaccine revenue is an unsuitable standalone measure of the whole field’s direction.

mainstream.scope: Routine use of additional RNA medicines in selected liver, cardiovascular and rare-disease indications, with approved vaccine extensions.
mainstream.rationale: Already approved RNA products validate parts of the platform. Broader routine use depends on delivery beyond the liver, manufacturing and indication-specific clinical benefit. Cancer vaccines and RNA editing remain conditional on trial outcomes.

metric.name: Alnylam annual net product revenue
metric.scope: RNA interference medicines sold by one company; excludes collaboration revenue
metric.limitations: RNAi commercial proxy, not all RNA therapeutics or vaccines. Revenue reflects indication expansion, pricing and product mix; it is not a count of patients. Do not extend this series to imply mRNA vaccine sales followed the same path.
metric.futureNote: A separate Alnylam 2030 total-revenue CAGR ambition is included. Its scope differs from historical net product revenue and from the overall RNA market.

milestones.text: Alnylam reported $662.1 million in net product revenue for 2021.
No comparable 2022 revenue point is included in this extract.
The annual filing reports $1.241 billion in product revenue for 2023.
The same measure reached $1.646 billion in 2024.
Product revenue reached $2.987 billion as the commercial RNAi portfolio expanded.
February 2026 results document the 2025 full year; this is not a 2026 annual revenue forecast.

tailwinds: Sequence-based design can reuse development platforms
Established RNAi medicines provide commercial validation
Delivery and manufacturing suppliers benefit across multiple programmes
bottlenecks: Delivery to the intended tissue remains a central constraint
Durability, repeat dosing and tolerability differ by modality
Vaccine demand and policy can diverge from therapeutic growth
watchMetrics: Patients treated and reimbursed indication expansions
Clinical success by modality: siRNA, antisense, mRNA and RNA editing
Tissue delivery, dose burden and manufacturing yield

forwardInterpretation: The maturity path is an analyst scenario for the stated market scope. A score of 4 means routine use in that scope, not a measured adoption percentage. The window can shift if the listed cost, performance, evidence or policy bottlenecks fail to clear.
